SMOTE-family oversampling of latent vectors from a BiLSTM VAE used as an encoder, an existing sampler in a learned space; only classifiers are evaluated.

K-means cluster-based over- and undersampling plus Tomek-link undersampling, a chain of existing parts with no stated change; compared with other resampling methods.

Presents improved non-clustered and cluster-based oversampling techniques for big data on Hadoop without describing the change, which counts as own; the nod to prior oversampling work is not a stated comparison.

NICE builds minority counterfactuals by propensity-score matching of real feature values on causal features, then filters them, a generator of its own; compared with widely used and counterfactual-based imbalance methods.

MLDM, a diffusion model tailored to generate multilabel instances, a modified generative model; compared with other multilabel resampling algorithms.

LICIC, a new kernel-PCA oversampler that creates instances from less important components; compared with ROS, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.
Hybrid sampling with an LSTM-cBiGAN oversampler and a new time-series nearest-neighbour undersampler (TSFNN) of its own; compared with other benchmark sampling methods.
GM4OS co-evolves the oversampling function and the minority pairs with genetic programming and a genetic algorithm, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE.
Proposes three quantum-inspired QSMOTE variants used with PGM classifiers, new SMOTE variants; compared only with a random forest baseline.
Uses a one-dimensional DCGAN to oversample mitotic patterns in a CNN feature space, a standard generator with no stated change; only improvement over no oversampling is reported.
SMOBD, a novel density-based oversampler combined with cost-sensitive SVM; compared with SMOTE and SMOTE-ENN.

Weighted online sequential ELM whose offline stage oversamples the minority within a principal-curve confidence region, an oversampler of its own; compared only with ELM variants.
Corr-OS synthesizes ectopic beats from the top-K correlated heartbeats, an oversampler of its own presented with a small CNN; compared with the Next-OS augmentation.

Region-partitioned oversampling with RBF undersampling, interpolation in the boundary region, affine shadowsampling in the safe region and class-potential screening, a new scheme; compared with other oversamplers.

Adaptive oversampling placed inside Boosting, Bagging and Random Subspace ensembles (ASOBoost) with no stated change to the sampler; compared with existing class imbalance learning methods that the abstract does not call resampling methods.

New oversampler using genetic-algorithm selection and crossover guided by feature selection; compared with SMOTE, ROS, RUS and no sampling.
KG-SMOTE inserts synthetic samples by a Gaussian distribution around K-means cluster nodes, a new SMOTE variant; results are only before against after.
New oversampler that runs SMOTE along paths of a minimum spanning tree built on a KNN graph of the minority class; no comparison with other resamplers is stated.

Standard GAN, VAE and CVAE oversamplers with posterior binarization of dummy features, mixed with SMOTE-type samples at a tunable ratio (Elastic Oversampling); no stated change to the generators; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-Tomek and ADASYN.

MCMO-Boost, a newly named oversampling algorithm built on AdaBoost whose change is not described, counts as own; compared with C4.5, AdaBoost and SMOTE.

A new genetic-algorithm oversampler that evolves optimized synthetic minority instances; compared with three existing sampling techniques.

3D-HyperGAMO, a new adversarial minority oversampling model that generates 3-D hyperspectral patches with a separate classifier; no comparison with resamplers is stated.
DDCO places synthetic samples using per-dimension data characteristics so they stay in the minority region, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and MWMOTE.
MCS-GMM draws Monte Carlo samples from a fitted GMM but weights minority instances by neighbours and density after a three-sigma split into four types, a changed sampler; compared with SMOTE.

Resampling degree set by a classification intensity computed with a base classifier, a new way of applying resampling; the abstract names no generator; compared only with unnamed traditional methods.
Functional random forest with cost-sensitive splitting whose hybrid sampling uses functional SMOTE and weighted bootstrapping as is; the contribution is the classifier.

OREM interpolates only inside clean subregions around minority samples, with a multiclass version and a boosting version, a new oversampler; no named comparison.
Generates minority log messages with a standard SeqGAN and no stated change; results only show that oversampling helps.

Has a pretrained language model progressively mask and impute majority rows toward the minority and self-authenticate labels, a new sampling procedure for the generator; no named comparison.

Hybrid CVAE and conditional WGAN with column-specific output heads for counts and zero-inflated columns, then boundary and novelty tests, a modified generator; compared with SMOTE.

FireMID uses the firefly metaheuristic as an oversampler after JMIM feature selection, an oversampler of its own; compared with traditional models and oversampling techniques.

Cost-sensitive majority-weighted minority oversampling that sets synthetic counts by imbalance ratio and weights borderline samples by distance and density, a changed oversampler; compared with unnamed imbalanced learning algorithms.

A standard VAE trained on few defective wafers generates synthetic trace data; the strategies studied concern the input representation, not the model; compared only between classifiers.

Oversamples faulty modules according to their fault content from the software history, a new way of setting how much to oversample; compared with traditional oversampling techniques.
Oversampling with a modified spectral clustering that sets how many samples to generate in each cluster, a new allocation; compared with k-means clustering-based oversampling.

A biased SOCP-SVM splits support and non-support vectors, then standard SMOTE on minority support vectors and repeated RUS on majority non-support vectors feed an SVM ensemble, a chain of existing parts; no named comparison.
Semi-supervised sleep EEG classifier that also improves SMOTE to remove mixed boundary samples, an improved SMOTE; results only before against after balancing.
New multi-label synthetic oversampler based on local label distribution; no named comparison.

Generates synthetic COVID samples in a deep feature space with a new algorithm for the scatter topology of the minor class and selective generation, a generator of its own; compared with other data augmentation methods.
A genetic-algorithm wrapper searches for regions in which random oversampling generates data, a new way of applying oversampling; compared with SMOTE and random oversampling.
SMOTE followed by a new intuitionistic fuzzy rough instance selection that cleans both classes, inside a data reduction method; the cleaner is the paper's own; no comparison is named.
SMOTE-MRS clusters with K-means, applies standard SMOTE in each cluster and tops up with random oversampling, a new name over existing parts; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-ENC and ROS.

Called a novel class-conditional latent diffusion model, but the abstract shows the standard design conditioned on CLIP text prompts of the class, plus selective oversampling; compared with no and traditional augmentation.

Proposes Adaptive-SMOTE, which selects Inner and Danger minority groups, and a Gaussian oversampler with dimension reduction, new oversamplers; compared with other sampling methods.
Oversamples only borderline, rare and outlier positives at different rates, a new allocation of synthetic examples; compared with ADASYN, SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.

BEFO ranks synthetic gene-expression samples against WGCNA co-expression clusters with random forests and keeps only those more important than real ones, a selection step of its own; compared with five oversampling methods.
Importance-SMOTE oversamples only borderline and edge minority samples in proportion to an importance score and places samples by relative importance, a changed SMOTE; no named comparison.
Standard CTGAN applied within multiple feature-selection views feeding an AutoML-weighted ensemble; the contribution is the intrusion detection pipeline; compared with intrusion detection methods.

Generates instances by perturbing random feature subsets of seeds, guided by a per-instance imbalance impact, inside an ensemble, a new oversampler; the reference methods are not said to be resamplers.
DAK-SMOTE stratifies minority samples by local outlier factor and adapts k, a changed SMOTE presented with a transformer; compared with traditional SMOTE.
PTASO uses Poincare distance, two-stage weights and region-specific generators (BEAS, OGS), a new oversampler; no named comparison.
HetGSMOTE extends SMOTE to heterogeneous graphs with node-type, edge-type and metapath information and type-specific edge generators, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed baselines.
Sliding-window minority sequences are generated by an improved VAE-GAN combination, a modified generator; compared with fault detection methods and oversampling techniques.

Feature selection approach for fault detection that proposes WSMOTE, a manifold-based weighted SMOTE; no comparison with other resamplers.
SeismoFlow is a Glow-inspired flow model that interpolates in its latent space, with no stated change to the model, an existing sampler in a learned space; only compared with no augmentation.

Grey-wolf-optimized K-means clustering followed by cluster-based oversampling, existing parts with no stated change; the benchmarking algorithms are not said to be resamplers.
Hybrid of SMOTE and bootstrap sampling in a one-versus-all setup for multiclass health data, existing parts; only variants of the method and classifiers are compared.
A novel adaptive data structure based oversampler for ordinal classes that synthesizes objects from the structure of minority classes; compared with existing techniques for synthetic objects.
Uses an LSTM sequence model, which the abstract treats as an existing generative model, to generate minority samples from parent sequences with no stated change; compared with SMOTE.

DSP-SMOTE undersamples easy majority and oversamples difficult minority examples by a two-way self-paced mechanism with hybrid difficulty, a new SMOTE variant; compared with previous SMOTE-related methods.

MI-SpikingGAN adds spiking neurons, low-frequency wrapping and feature-matching losses and attention-based fusion to the GAN, a new generator; the other methods compared are not said to be resamplers.
A novel semi-supervised adaptive elastic GAN for blood cell images, a new generative model; compared with the conventional semi-supervised WGAN.
Distribution-preserving resampling with a new redundancy-removing undersampler (RRUS) and a core-seed SMOTE (CS-SMOTE), both of its own; compared only with other classifiers.
FB-MIO oversamples by multiple imputation guided by a new missingness-density factor and oscillator, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and Borderline-SMOTE.
SMOTE-ANO-FLS adds new local-set noise detection, adaptive noise modification and probability weights to SMOTE, a changed SMOTE; compared with 7 oversampling methods.
S2MAID combines semi-supervised labelling with a density-based undersampler (UD-density) and a SMOTE-density oversampler of its own and an ensemble; no named comparison.
Generates synthetic samples and accepts or rejects each by its location, a new oversampler with a rejection rule; no explicit comparison with other resamplers.
HS-SMOTE scores sample points with regular hexagons and interpolates among several samples without k-nearest neighbours, a new SMOTE variant; compared with ten sampling methods.
Noise-aware extension of the quantum-inspired QSMOTE that perturbs its similarity estimation, a changed oversampler; compared with plain QSMOTE and no balancing.
Generates minority samples by perturbing majority samples under a counterfactual objective, a new oversampler; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
SMOTE plus ENN where the SMOTE rate is set by the out-of-bag error of two-factor random forests, a new way of setting how much to oversample; compared with a traditional sampling algorithm.
GAN-ASMOTE combines a standard GAN with adaptive SMOTE, with no stated change to the generator; no comparison is named.
MBK-SMOTE adds sample density and concentration-area division to SMOTE, an improved SMOTE; compared with standard and improved SMOTE.
MEXT, a parameter-free multiclass oversampler that places synthetic instances by anomalous scores and balances all classes at once; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN, Safe-Level SMOTE, MDO and DSRBF.
DNOS applies separate denoising processes of its own to majority and minority samples before ADASYN; compared with ADASYN.

LOF-Enhanced SMOTE removes boundary noise by LOF and uses a Gaussian kernel similarity in generation, a changed SMOTE; compared with SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.

VIGraph generates minority nodes with a variational graph autoencoder trained with cross-view contrastive learning, adjacency reconstruction and alignment, a modified generative model; no explicit comparison.
No abstract; the title names a new local-distribution weighted oversampler (MMWO), so unclear.
Synthesizes new steganalysis samples from both majority and minority samples, a new oversampler; compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN.
VANet introduces Weighted SMOTE, an improved SMOTE that sets sample counts by minority weights; compared only with other networks.
Proposes a new oversampling technique for imbalanced multilabel molecular graphs without describing it, so unclear; compared with MLSMOTE.
Credit rating model with SMOTE and a clustering-improved boundary-sensitive undersampling feeding a dynamic ensemble, existing parts; no named comparison.

SD-KMSMOTE filters noise, clusters minority samples and gives informative sub-clusters larger weights and more synthetic samples, a new oversampler; the existing methods compared are not said to be resamplers.

A new twice-SVM undersampler that deletes majority samples far from the hyperplane, combined with an unnamed oversampler, a scheme of its own; tested only on artificial data without a resampler comparison.
ABS, a newly named sampler that generates synthetic data from concatenated features, with a boosting version (ABSBoost); compared only with a previous study not said to be a resampler.
CORE oversamples the core of the minority and undersamples borderline majority by safe levels, a new hybrid sampler; no named comparison.
EC-WGAN is a conditional WGAN-GP with 1D convolutions in place of dense layers, standard parts under a new name; only its own effectiveness is reported.
CMCOB interpolates within maximal cliques of a cosine nearest-neighbour graph with central and radial boundary strategies, a new multiclass oversampler; compared with multiclass oversampling methods.
Credit risk model whose Borderline-SMOTE generates adaptive numbers per boundary sample with a new interpolation, a changed SMOTE; compared with unnamed methods.
BE-G-SMOTE clusters faults with a GMM, weights clusters by a density function and tunes an SVM-based boundary, a changed SMOTE; no named comparison.
LS-SMOTE filters noise with local sets and interpolates toward the sample closest to the majority within each local set, a new SMOTE variant; compared with representative oversamplers.
Uses Gabriel graphs inside Borderline-SMOTE to find borderline samples without a free parameter, a changed SMOTE; compared with standard Borderline-SMOTE.
CycleGAN generates fault samples and a K-means SMOTE plus DCGAN chain enlarges them, standard generators under a new name; no comparison is named.
AKDRSMOTE adds adaptive k and dynamic random disturbance to SMOTE, a changed SMOTE presented with an IHHO-optimized SVM; compared only with fault detection techniques.
DepAug disentangles prosody and semantics with two encoders and a decoder that generates synthetic speech samples, a generator of its own; compared with supervised and self-supervised models.
The same borderline oversampling applied in the kernel's empirical feature space, an existing sampler in a learned space; compared with that method in the input space.
A standard conditional GAN generates multivariate flare time series; compared with oversampling, undersampling and synthetic oversampling.
HHO-SMOTe uses Harris hawk optimization to find the SMOTE sampling rate for each dataset, a search for how much to oversample; no resampler comparison.
The CRD module clusters to find minority samples that resemble the majority and oversamples only those, a new allocation of its own though the oversampler is not named; only ablations.
Applies SMOTE, SMOTE-Tomek, KMeans-SMOTE and ADASYN as is within a tree of random forests with rule-based fusion; the contribution is the classifier framework.
BGCS models pairwise dependencies of binary features with a Gaussian copula tailored to binary data, then filters with a GPT-2 classifier; compared with SMOTE, CTGAN and the standard Gaussian copula.

A novel oversampler based on local density distributions for protein interaction sites; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
